summary: Computes a projected signed distance by fetching a position-monitor struct via PositionChangeMonitor, differencing two position pointers to form a direction vector, and projecting the vehicle's position offsets (this+0x34D4/0x34D8/0x34DC) against the monitor origin along the normalized direction, added to a stored distance. Returns the stored distance directly when the direction vector is zero, and clamps the result with flt_5EA3FC[0] (floor at 0.0 / ceiling at the threshold).

operations.description: v2 = PositionChangeMonitor(this) returns the position-monitor struct
load two position pointers from the monitor (p1 = *(v2+272), p0 = *(v2+268)) and form the direction vector v8 = p1[0]-p0[0], v9 = p1[1]-p0[1], v10 = p1[2]-p0[2]
if v8 == 0.0 and v9 == 0.0 and v10 == 0.0 (zero direction), return the stored distance *(float*)(v2+72) directly
normalize the direction: v6 = 1/sqrt(v10*v10 + v9*v9 + v8*v8); v11 = v8*v6; v12 = v9*v6

v7 = projected distance = dot(normalized direction, vehicle offset - monitor origin) + stored distance: v6*v10*(this+0x34DC - *(float*)(v2+8)) + v12*(this+0x34D8 - *(float*)(v2+4)) + v11*(this+0x34D4 - *(float*)(v2+0)) + *(float*)(v2+72)
clamp v7 against flt_5EA3FC[0]: if negative, v7 += flt_5EA3FC[0] and return 0.0 if still negative; if greater than the threshold, v7 -= flt_5EA3FC[0] and return the threshold if still above it

clean_pseudocode: else if (proj > flt_5EA3FC[0]) { proj -= flt_5EA3FC[0]; if (proj > flt_5EA3FC[0]) return flt_5EA3FC[0]; }
